summary: research studies reach main in two PRs: the protocol on its own before the first search, then the report
appCreator: With the research module, every study now arrives as two pull requests: a small one with the plan (the protocol and its row in the index of studies) that is merged before any search starts, then one with the report. In a repo where only you merge, the search waits until you have merged the first one.

The plan's own commit on main is what proves the pass and fail rules were fixed before the search. Before, a study merged as one squashed commit lost that proof, and the skill never said how a study gets to main at all.
The skeptic agent now checks that order on main, and that the plan changed afterwards only in its Deviations section.

branch.none: checked by hand at the #350 checkpoints

notVerified: No studio-scratch live check (1.0 batch rule: checked by hand at the #350 checkpoints). No real study was run end to end and no real PR was opened by the skill.

The skill was tested with one dry-run prompt on Sonnet (a user reality check): it planned two PRs with the right titles and contents, the first search after the protocol PR merged, and waiting for the App Creator in an owner-merged repo. Not repeated, and other branches and the deep tier were not tried.

The skeptic's git check was run by hand on a toy repository (it passes the two-PR flow before and after the report merges, and flags a study squashed into one commit); the skeptic agent itself was not run.
